scope: Public scientific calculations, bundled numerical defaults, conservation contracts, and scientific data interfaces in exergy-imperative 0.7.0

items.title: Dependency-free thermodynamic kernels
limitations: Chemical exergy requires an explicit composition-specific factor or a separate reference-state model.
Heat-service factors are boundary equations, not equipment performance predictions.

items.title: Energy units, temperature parsing, basis protection, and dead-state validation

evidence.title: NIST Guide to the SI, Appendix B

limitations: HHV-to-LHV conversion is intentionally rejected unless the caller supplies a fuel-specific relationship.
A reference environment declares a dead state; it does not infer atmospheric chemical composition.

items.title: CoolProp physical-flow exergy backend

evidence.title: CoolProp documentation
evidence.locator: state-property backend independently compared with steam-table and ideal-gas cases

limitations: Accuracy follows the selected CoolProp fluid model and valid state region.
Mixtures, reactions, and chemical exergy are outside this backend.

items.title: Progressive-fidelity carrier, service, and technology assessment
limitations: Chemical-fuel factors and technology efficiencies are broad screening values unless explicitly supplied.
The library does not infer site performance, composition, or operating state.

items.title: Declared-boundary exergy balances
limitations: Inferred destruction is valid only when every product and loss crossing the declared boundary is represented.
A negative closure is retained as a residual and is never reported as negative destruction.

items.title: Connected energy/exergy systems and time series

evidence.title: First- and second-law network identities
evidence.locator: internal flows cancel at the aggregate boundary

limitations: Positive storage accumulation is represented as a balance-equivalent product and release as a balance-equivalent input; the explicit accumulation field preserves the signed state change.
The model does not solve thermodynamic states or transient dynamics.

items.title: Material, constituent, and declared chemical-exergy ledgers
limitations: This is a ledger, not a reaction-equilibrium or stoichiometric solver.
Chemical exergy is calculated only when every stream has an explicit specific factor.
Storage accumulation uses the same balance-equivalent input/product convention as connected energy systems.

items.title: Explicit-performance technology relations

evidence.title: Technology model contract
evidence.locator: input multiplied by user-declared performance and exergy factors

limitations: Models do not predict efficiency, COP, state, composition, degradation, or site behavior.
Residual exergy combines destruction and unallocated losses.

items.title: Heat pump, refrigeration, furnace, and waste-heat screens

evidence.title: US DOE Process Heating System Sourcebook

limitations: Heat-pump source temperature acts as the dead-state reservoir; non-environmental heat sources need an explicit connected-system boundary.
Furnace useful heat is an isothermal service approximation; detailed audits need material and fluid states.
Waste-heat matching is a greedy feasibility screen, not pinch analysis or heat-exchanger design.

items.title: Steam and compressed-air engineering screens

evidence.title: US DOE Improving Compressed Air System Performance

limitations: Compressed-air useful-energy and energy-efficiency fields use reversible pressure exergy as the service proxy; use the exergy fields for interpretation.
Steam exergy is an isothermal heat-service approximation unless the property backend is used.
Defaults are not measured boiler or compressor performance.

items.title: GWP and stationary-combustion emission factors

evidence.title: US EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub 2025

limitations: Default fuel factors are inventory defaults, not stack measurements.
Pollutant factors produce inventories with qualitative health context, not dispersion, exposure, dose-response, or health-risk estimates.
Aggregate grid CO2e cannot be separated into gas-specific 20- and 100-year totals.

items.title: EPA regional outdoor-air public-health benefit screening

evidence.title: U.S. EPA Public Health Benefits per Kilowatt-Hour, Third Edition
evidence.locator: Table 2, 2023 BPK values for 14 AVERT regions and eight intervention types

evidence.title: U.S. EPA BPK use and limitations
evidence.locator: screening use, methods, boundaries, currency year, discount rate, and suggested analysis-year window

limitations: The values monetize modeled PM2.5- and ozone-related outdoor-air benefits; they do not predict local exposure, diagnoses, individual risk, or facility-specific health incidence.
The model domain is the contiguous United States, and benefits attributed to a source AVERT region include effects modeled outside that region.
The values use 2023 power-sector, emissions, population, baseline-incidence, income, and valuation inputs and a 2 percent discount rate; EPA suggests using them only for 2018-2028 analyses.
The arithmetic midpoint is a library presentation value, not an additional EPA estimate; decisions should retain and report the published low/high range.

items.title: Bundled country-year electricity factors

evidence.title: Our World in Data electricity data
evidence.locator: bundled snapshot records source version and retrieval date

limitations: The bundled table is a versioned historical snapshot and must not be treated as a current marginal or hourly grid factor.
Country averages do not establish a site-specific contractual or consequential electricity boundary.

items.title: GHG boundary accounting and methane disposition
limitations: Default methane density is pure methane at 0 C and 101.325 kPa; actual gas composition and standard conditions must replace it.
Default recovery and oxidation efficiencies are screening bounds, not field measurements.
Lifecycle upstream and downstream emissions are included only when explicitly modeled.

items.title: Discounted cash flow and technology economics
limitations: Correct arithmetic does not validate prices, escalation, tax, financing, project life, residual value, or decision boundary.
IRR is suppressed for cash flows with possible multiple-root ambiguity.

items.title: Monte Carlo, sensitivity, EVPI, and scenario arithmetic

evidence.title: Probability and decision-analysis identities
evidence.locator: distribution moments, rank correlation, and paired-sample EVPI

limitations: Output validity depends on the user's distribution choices, correlations, model form, and scenario completeness.
Bounded normal sampling is rejection-sampled from a truncated normal, not clipped at the bounds.

items.title: Degree days, climatology, anomalies, and weather normalization
limitations: The regression is a transparent degree-day screen, not an IPMVP-compliant baseline by itself.
Reference-period selection, occupancy, production, autocorrelation, and model diagnostics remain the analyst's responsibility.

items.title: Process templates and opportunity priors
limitations: Savings fractions are broad author-defined screening priors, not statistically validated project distributions.
A process opportunity is not a guaranteed saving, audit result, or equipment recommendation.

items.title: Oil and gas, emerging-energy, advanced-materials, and sector packs

evidence.title: Pack provenance contracts
evidence.locator: each source requires title, license, and applicable boundary

evidence.title: U.S. DOE FEMP geothermal heat-pump acquisition guidance
evidence.locator: COP procurement table and ISO 13256-1 example boundary

evidence.title: U.S. DOE vehicle efficiency Fact of the Week 1360
evidence.locator: 87-91% stored-energy-to-wheels EV range including regenerative braking

evidence.title: U.S. DOE CHP gas-turbine fact sheet
evidence.locator: Table 2 natural-gas HHV to net-electric efficiency cases

evidence.title: U.S. DOE NETL natural-gas compression field tests
U.S. DOE liquid alkaline electrolysis targets
evidence.locator: 2022 system status and ultimate LHV efficiency target

evidence.title: NREL/TP-5700-79806
evidence.locator: round-trip efficiency comparison for flow batteries and pumped-thermal storage

limitations: Published priors are F1 screening estimates with narrow declared applicability; they are not measurements, fleet distributions, site guarantees, or design values.
Energy-performance results intentionally omit exergy when heat state or fuel quality is not known; mass-normalized intensity is not conversion efficiency.
Profiles without a boundary-compatible published range remain discovery metadata and required-input contracts.
Pack validation proves schema, provenance, ranges, arithmetic, and override behavior, not empirical applicability to a user asset.

items.title: NASA POWER, ERA5-Land, eGRID, EDGAR, FIED, IAC, and World Bank interfaces

evidence.title: Publisher-owned source datasets
evidence.locator: local adapters preserve publisher version, boundary, units, and provenance

limitations: Interface tests use local fixtures and do not certify changing publisher data.
The caller must inspect publisher metadata, licensing, revisions, geography, units, and time basis.

items.title: Record preprocessing and quantity-quality interoperability

evidence.title: XAI4Heat paper reproduction contract
evidence.locator: optional user-supplied records are compared with published portfolio aggregates

limitations: Column mapping and arithmetic validation do not establish sensor accuracy, interval completeness, or representativeness.
The underlying XAI4Heat telemetry is not redistributed by this project.

items.title: Agent, CLI, MCP, schema, and reporting surfaces

evidence.title: Stable contract tests
evidence.locator: JSON Schemas, exit codes, in-memory MCP client, and deterministic serialization

limitations: Interface correctness inherits the scientific assurance level of the invoked calculation.
Reports do not upgrade screening inputs into measurements or design results.

notes: No capability is globally labeled decision-grade: that status requires validated site boundaries, calibrated measurements, uncertainty appropriate to the decision, and qualified engineering review.
Reference-validated means agreement for the listed equations, constants, source values, boundaries, and tolerances; it is not universal empirical validation.
Screening-only and external-data-required entries are deliberately visible so passing software tests cannot be mistaken for scientific validation.
